How many fancy spa products are made from of everyday kitchen items.

Could you list those items and the ratios of said items in certain products.

I need the information for reasons. Definitely not to start my own half price bed bath and beyond though. That's for sure.

I would love to share!

Any ingredient I mention should be available in your local grocery or health food store. Too lazy to go look for them? I've had great luck buying small quantities of ingredients on eBay. These are all products I have made and used in spas during my 15 years as a massage therapist. These treatments go for big bucks, and are simple to recreate at home.

A very effective clay mask is bentonite clay and water. You can apply clay to your face, hair, and body. The ratio of clay to water is based on your personal preference. For face clay, I like it thin enough I can apply it with a fan brush. For the body, I prefer it thicker- like margarine. Important note- do not make this ahead of time. Some homemade stuff can go bad quickly because there are no preservatives, so only preparing enough for one use is suggested for this one.

A salt or sugar scrub is made with granulated sugar or granulated salt plus oil. I prefer coarse salt, because i prefer a rough scrub. I like the texture of my scrub to feel like greasy sand, but make what feels good to you. I suggest using oils such as almond, grapeseed or coconut, but any type of oil in your pantry will work. If you want to personalize the scrub, add essential oils. There are blends you can make (or buy) for detoxification, relaxation, stress relief, etc. It is a great treatment for dry elbows, knees and heels. This one has a long shelf life. Scrubs are made this way at lots of spas.

~~~Please do your homework on essential oils before using them! Make sure they are safe for you! For example, basil essential oil can cause seizures in epileptics. Many essential oils are contraindicated during pregnancy. ~~~

You can make a fantastic whipped body butter from cocoa butter, shea butter and jojoba oil. You can use any combination of butters and oils. There are so many different ones! Avocado oil, mango butter, vitamin E oil, etc. they're all great for your skin! Experiment to find a combination you like! Melt the solids, mix with the liquids. You want about 75% butters and 25% oils. Put it in the fridge for a bit, until it solidifies most of the way, then throw it in your mixer and whip it until it doubles in volume. It is light and fluffy, but rich. At one spa this was the body butter we used after the clay body wrap.

Epsom salts are amazing, and cheap! You actually absorb magnesium from soaking in them! Grab a big bag of plain epsom salts for just a few bucks! Add essential oils, if you'd like. I used to work at a place that charged $20 for a mineral bath. For $20, you could buy enough of those minerals to last you for dozens of baths- it was equal parts sea salt, epsom salt and baking soda.

These are a few off the top of my head, feel free to ask any questions you might have! I'm happy to dish spa secrets lol. Pinterest is an excellent resource for DIY spa info as well :)

Not necessarily common knowledge per se, but a friend in the hospitality industry told me this about wines: On a given menu, the wine they sell by far the most of is the House, and it stands to reason - cheapest etc. Therefore, most places pick a good wine for the House red/white, and not as great a one for second and third down the menu (the more expensive ones).

There's also a lot of rotation when it comes to House wines, they go through a lot of bottles, and thus you're more likely to get a freshly opened bottle than one not (again, from a friend - most places are supposed to date when bottles are opened and to stop serving the wine within a few days - lots of places don't do this. There's a chance your chosen bottle of wine is a week+ old).
